topic: Lucas Geometry: 27 Nodes, Polarity, and Sheets
audience: High-school seniors; first-principles teaching, with concrete prerequisite capabilities and taught bridges.
prerequisites: Signed arithmetic, fractions, ratios, powers, linear equations, and coordinate graphs
learning_outcomes: List the 27 signed-address nodes without duplicates
Map a node through the half-basis rule with an explicit origin
Count the seven sheet populations and verify their total
Compute node polarity without merging distinct meanings of parity
Separate 26 noncentral nodes from 13 unoriented pairs
Construct a registry retaining addresses, positions, sheet labels, and signs
requested_deliverables: capstone.md with full answers and rubric
assumptions: A topical short course, not a semester per topic. Pacing is 55-minute core lessons plus capstone periods; split dense lessons if actual learner load requires it.
No prior calculus, abstract algebra, university linear algebra, or quantum mechanics unless explicitly taught earlier.
Required core assessments must be solvable with taught finite examples. Clearly label deeper recognition-only extensions.
Markdown is the delivery format; no PDF or Word generation is required.

course_map.title: Enumerating the balanced node window
course_map.worked_example_capability: List the 27 signed-address nodes without duplicates
course_map.assessment_target: List the 27 signed-address nodes without duplicates

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach Cartesian-product enumeration with three nested lists, the product rule for counts, and duplicate checking; code is optional.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Enumerate L in {-1,0,1}^3 by fixing L1, then L2, then L3. Nine rows per fixed L1 gives 27 unique rows.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: Enumerate the nine rows with L1=0. Classify full registry by nonzero-coordinate count: 0->1, 1->6, 2->12, 3->8.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Explain why 3+3+3 is not the count and verify 1+6+12+8=27.

teaching_anchor.production_rule: Expand this anchor diagnostic to 3–5 diagnostic checks; teach all operations before use. Split the lesson if these activities exceed 55 minutes.

course_map.title: Node addresses versus physical positions
course_map.worked_example_capability: Map a node through the half-basis rule with an explicit origin
course_map.assessment_target: Map a node through the half-basis rule with an explicit origin

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Distinguish node label L, half-address L/2, physical position, and half-open cell owner. Boundary nodes need not belong to the origin cell.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: L=(1,0,0) gives p=(5/2,-1,4), q1=1/2, cell owner z=(1,0,0), although it is a node of the centered window.

teaching_anchor.production_rule: Expand this anchor diagnostic to 3–5 diagnostic checks; teach all operations before use. Split the lesson if these activities exceed 55 minutes.

course_map.title: Lambda sheets and population counts
course_map.worked_example_capability: Count the seven sheet populations and verify their total
course_map.assessment_target: Count the seven sheet populations and verify their total

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define lambda as an integer sum. Count by explicit rows before mentioning a generating polynomial; the polynomial is recognition-only.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Count lambda=-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3 populations as 1,3,6,7,6,3,1. For lambda=0 list center plus six permutations of (1,0,-1).

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For lambda=2 list (1,1,0),(1,0,1),(0,1,1). For lambda=1 list three permutations of (1,0,0) and three of (1,1,-1).

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Verify total 27 and mirrored populations; show that L and -L have opposite lambda. With g_lambda=(1,0,-1/3), verify g_lambda dot (p-O)=lambda/2 for L=(1,-1,1).

teaching_anchor.production_rule: Expand this anchor diagnostic to 3–5 diagnostic checks; teach all operations before use. Split the lesson if these activities exceed 55 minutes.

course_map.title: Parity and directed signs
course_map.worked_example_capability: Compute node polarity without merging distinct meanings of parity
course_map.assessment_target: Compute node polarity without merging distinct meanings of parity

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define even/odd integers including negative integers and chi=(-1)^lambda. Distinguish a parity label from a directed vector sign; no complex exponential is required.

worked_example.task_and_answer: L=(1,-1,1) has lambda=1, chi=-1; L=(1,1,0) has lambda=2, chi=+1.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: L=(-1,-1,-1) has lambda=-3 and chi=-1; center has chi=+1. Count chi=+1 rows=13, chi=-1 rows=14.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: L and -L have equal chi even though lambda and displacement reverse. Explain why chi does not recover orientation.

teaching_anchor.production_rule: Expand this anchor diagnostic to 3–5 diagnostic checks; teach all operations before use. Split the lesson if these activities exceed 55 minutes.

mod_three_bridge.introduce: Define lambda mod3 as its remainder0,1,2, using lambda=3k+r with integer k and0<=r<3. This is different from even/odd parity.
mod_three_bridge.worked: lambda=-2 has mod3 class1 and chi=+1; lambda=1 has the same class1 but chi=-1.
mod_three_bridge.practice: lambda=-1 has class2, chi=-1; lambda=2 has class2, chi=+1. Count nine nodes in each mod3 class from the seven sheet counts.
mod_three_bridge.diagnostic: The seven sheet populations give three mod3 populations9,9,9 but two chi populations13,14. Neither class label nor chi determines directed L. Retain each field separately.

course_map.title: Antipodal pairs and observation rules
course_map.worked_example_capability: Separate 26 noncentral nodes from 13 unoriented pairs
course_map.assessment_target: Separate 26 noncentral nodes from 13 unoriented pairs

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Define an antipodal pair as an equivalence class and choose a canonical representative whose first nonzero component is positive. Store an orientation sign to invert the quotient.

worked_example.task_and_answer: For L=(-1,0,1), representative v=(1,0,-1), sign s=-1, L=s*v. The 26 nonzero rows give 13 pairs; center is a separate singleton.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: L=(0,-1,-1) gives v=(0,1,1), s=-1; its partner has s=+1. Reconstruct both physical points and show their sum is 2O.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: A pair label alone cannot recover directed L. Keep s and treat the center separately; do not assign it two orientations.

teaching_anchor.production_rule: Expand this anchor diagnostic to 3–5 diagnostic checks; teach all operations before use. Split the lesson if these activities exceed 55 minutes.

course_map.title: A complete finite registry
course_map.worked_example_capability: Construct a registry retaining addresses, positions, sheet labels, and signs
course_map.assessment_target: Construct a registry retaining addresses, positions, sheet labels, and signs

teaching_anchor.bridge_to_teach: Teach registry column meanings and independent checks; retain all 27 rows rather than only totals or paired summaries.

worked_example.task_and_answer: Build columns L,q,p,lambda,chi,pair representative,orientation sign. For (1,-1,1): q=(1/2,-1/2,1/2), p=(2,-2,5/2), lambda=1, chi=-1, representative=(1,-1,1), sign=+1.

guided_practice.task_and_answer: For (-1,1,-1): p=(2,0,11/2), lambda=-1, chi=-1, same representative and sign=-1. Reconstruct each row.

diagnostic.task_and_answer: Check unique L count 27, sheet counts 1,3,6,7,6,3,1, 13 noncentral pairs plus center, and inverse physical mapping for every row.

teaching_anchor.production_rule: Expand this anchor diagnostic to 3–5 diagnostic checks; teach all operations before use. Split the lesson if these activities exceed 55 minutes.

capstone_specification.task: Produce and verify a complete 27-node registry and explain which information an antipodal quotient retains or removes.
required_operations: Enumerate all27 unique signed triples; reconcile vertex/edge/face/center counts.
Map every node to a physical point with L/2 and the declared origin; explain one boundary ownership case.
Tabulate seven lambda populations and verify one affine sheet identity.
Compute every chi label and explain why antipodal orientation and chi differ.
Store13 canonical noncentral pairs, orientation sign per row and the separate center; reconstruct directed labels.
Deliver the complete registry and run counts, pair and inverse-mapping checks without deleting rows.
Add a separate mod3 field to the registry and reconcile its9,9,9 counts with seven sheets and two chi classes.
